answer.summary: Livingston’s advice was to deliberately pay attention during founder conversations: notice subtle interpersonal and commitment cues rather than rely on trick questions. [S1, S3]

sections.heading: What to watch for
sections.content: Before meeting founders, remind yourself that you’re evaluating how they work together and how committed they are. Notice whether co-founders seem to get along, whether founders understand and care about their product, and whether their actions match claims such as being ready to leave a job. She also said defensiveness was a bad sign. [S1, S3, S4]

sections.heading: How to build the skill
sections.content: Have a conversation and pay attention to subtle cues; Livingston said there are no trick questions to ask. Treat warning signs as prompts to pay closer attention, rather than as automatic conclusions. [S1, S6]

judgment.explanation: The answer accurately captures her advice to pay attention to subtle cues, including whether co-founders get along, founders’ grasp of their product, and defensiveness. But it omits her suggestion to ask about the founders’ history together—such as how they met and whether they had worked together before—so it does not cover all expected points.
